newsitem.title: UK: LPC - Greece mulls jumbo refinancing.
newsitem.headline: LPC - Greece mulls jumbo refinancing.

text.p: LONDON, January 22 (LPC) - Greece may seek more than $1 billion in loans from international banks, according to a Bank of Greece official.

Greece is looking to "renegotiate its 1994 and 1995 loans since the pricing can no longer be justified," said Spyros Papanicolau, Director of the International Banking Department at the Bank of Greece.

In July of 1994, the republic signed a $500 million, five year term loan provided by a syndicate of international banks and in April 1995 followed that up with a $600 million, five year facility. Both credits were priced at 80 bps over LIBOR.

Since then, pricing for Greek borrowers has fallen substantially, as an oversupply of capital amongst banks has driven syndicated loan rates down throughout Europe. In August the republic signed a $600 million loan, also for five years, at greatly reduced pricing. That deal had an initial margin of 45 bps, stepping up to 50 bps over LIBOR for the final two years.

Mr. Papanicolau said a decision on the refinancing would be made next week, after which banks would be asked to submit bids on the deal. He added that the republic might well be back OPEN QUOTE later in the year to refinance the 1996 loan CLOSE QUOTE as well as possibly looking for additional money.
